title: Separating Fact from Fiction: AI Does Not Set Prices at McDonald’s

reading.body:
The reporting here is a dispute about what a system does, not a documented account of it doing something. A class action complaint alleges that an AI-powered menu system was used to fix prices, and the company published a response denying that AI sets its prices. The underlying facts of how the pricing system operates are not established by these reports.

The failure mode, if the allegation holds, would be a system used outside the conditions it was built for, or a pricing tool whose outputs were treated as decisions rather than inputs. That is a claim in a complaint, not a finding. The company's own account of how it sets prices is a statement by an interested party, not an independent verification.

Catching this kind of thing would require visibility into what the pricing system actually controls and what human review sits between its output and a posted price. None of the three reports establishes that either way. The complaint is an allegation, the company statement is a denial, and neither is a ruling.
